bug_semantics: MiniServ treats any simplified request path matching the default unauth regex ^[A-Za-z0-9\-/_]+\.conf$ as pre-auth static content. handle_request does $simple =~ /$u/ over that allowlist and, on match, sets validated=4 and serves the file from the Webmin root with no session. Because the character class includes '/', an unauthenticated network client can GET any *.conf under module directories in the install root (not a single known public asset). CWE-185/CWE-777: the allowlist regex is incorrect and under-constrained for an authentication gate.
flaw_origin: The default vital-config unauth string that includes the .conf alternative, and the $simple =~ /$u/ matcher that honors it, were first written in miniserv.pl in GitHub commit fc1c1b243f7973c222c0b3a2d1f0ab45af485397 (Jamie Cameron, 2007-04-12, 'Initial checkin of Webmin'). Immediate parent 27d3d6cb9738150bc944ae17ebe8fc8a6396012e is only a test checkin of file/ and mailboxes/ Java modules and has no miniserv.pl and no unauth allowlist. Later edits (2009 '_' in the class; 2026 extraction into miniserv-lib.pl) did not first-write the mechanism.

Attack path: GET /<module>/<name>.conf against MiniServ (default port 10000) with no cookie; $page is percent-decoded then simplify_path'd to $simple; the .conf regex matches; file body is returned from the Webmin module directory (install root, not /etc/webmin). Shipped example: nis/nisupdate.conf.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-56021 is a live PUBLISHED CISA-CG record for unauthenticated MiniServ reads of module-directory *.conf files via a bad allowlist regex (CWE-185/CWE-777). The sink is the default unauth token ^[A-Za-z0-9\-/_]+\.conf$ consumed by $simple =~ /$u/ before any session check. CISA VA-26-169-02 v2.0.0 still marks all versions known_affected with no_fix_planned; HEAD still carries the token, so this is unpatched rather than fixed in 2.641. The GHSA/NVD 2.641 links are sibling-CVE copy-paste (that tag hardens SSL-header trust and /^success$/i, not .conf access). Vendor security.html for 2.641 does not list this issue, but CVE.org is not rejected, so the advisory is a real vulnerability, not FALSE_POSITIVE. BIC: git log -S / -L and parent-tree checks put the first write of both the .conf allowlist and the matcher in fc1c1b243f7973c222c0b3a2d1f0ab45af485397. That commit is a bulk 'Initial checkin of Webmin', but its parent is present and verifiable and contains no miniserv.pl; no finer public member (CVS/SF) could be reconstructed from this clone, so the first-write surviving git object is the BIC (not the 2009 '_' widening and not the 2026 library move). AI judgment is from that commit object only: Jamie Cameron author and committer, 2007-04-12, no AI trailers or bot identity → NOT_AI. Closed as unpatched NOT_AI with potential_fix recorded; remaining_gap names the missing upstream fix.
remaining_gap: unpatched: no upstream commit removes the MiniServ .conf unauth allowlist; CISA still records no_fix_planned and HEAD miniserv-lib.pl:3928 still contains ^[A-Za-z0-9\-/_]+\.conf$.

unpatched.reason: CISA VA-26-169-02 v2.0.0 (2026-08-11) lists CVE-2026-56021 as known_affected for vers:all/* with remediations no_fix_planned; git grep on HEAD and tag 2.641 still shows the .conf token in the default unauth allowlist, and git log -S finds no later deletion of that mechanism.

potential_fix.approach: Remove the ^[A-Za-z0-9\-/_]+\.conf$ token from MiniServ's default unauth vital-config (miniserv-lib.pl update_vital_config) and from any installed miniserv.conf unauth= line; keep only tightly anchored public paths such as ^/unauthenticated/ and explicit static image/js assets, matching the full simplified path with \A...\z rather than a searchable ^...$.
potential_fix.rationale: The disclosure sink is the unauth matcher treating any module-relative *.conf path as pre-auth static content. Dropping that pattern (or replacing it with an explicit allowlist of known public files) makes GET /<module>/*.conf require a session, which closes the unauthenticated file-read.
